before.title: 12.3-inch Infotainment / Lexus Interface Screen Freezing, Rebooting, or Going Blank
before.description: Owners of the current-generation LX have reported the center infotainment display freezing, rebooting, losing audio functions, or going black temporarily. Complaints and forum posts describe navigation, camera, and climate-related interface interruptions, sometimes resolved only by an ignition cycle or software update. The problem appears tied to head-unit software instability rather than a single hardware defect in many cases.
before.solution: Confirm software version and check for Lexus multimedia service bulletins or over-the-air/dealer updates. If the issue persists, dealers typically perform head-unit software reprogramming, inspect battery voltage and module communication faults, and replace the display/audio head unit only if updates do not resolve the problem. Owners should record when the failure occurs, especially if wireless phone projection is active.
symptoms: Backup or surround-view camera delayed or unavailable
Climate controls on screen become unresponsive

communityRecommendations.content: Owners commonly recommend updating the multimedia software first and temporarily disabling wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto if crashes are frequent.
If the screen goes blank intermittently, capture a video showing loss of camera or climate access to help the dealer justify module replacement.

proposal.title: 12.3-inch Infotainment / Lexus Interface Screen Freezing, Rebooting, or Going Blank
proposal.description: Lexus bulletin L-SB-0006-23 Rev1 covers 2022-2023 LX600 vehicles and documents head-unit black or white screens, flicker, freezes, reboots and phone-projection problems addressed by software. The bulletin explicitly says its black, flickering or frozen display conditions do not affect the backup camera. A separate VIN-specific recall, 25V744, covers a rearview-camera image that may freeze or fail to display on certain 2022-2025 LX vehicles because of Parking Assist ECU software. These are distinct conditions, and current primary evidence does not extend the head-unit bulletin itself to 2024-2025 LX vehicles.
proposal.solution: For center-display or phone-projection symptoms, record the behavior and have a Lexus-capable technician confirm the exact vehicle software version and bulletin applicability before updating the head unit. For a frozen or missing rearview image, check the VIN for recall 25V744 and obtain the free Parking Assist ECU software remedy if applicable. Do not infer that either condition requires display or head-unit replacement without diagnosis. These are bulletin- and VIN-specific dealer software remedies; no universal retail part is asserted.

before.title: AHC (Active Height Control) Suspension Failure
before.description: The Active Height Control hydraulic suspension on the LX570 develops leaks in the height control actuators, accumulator, and hydraulic lines. The system uses hydraulic fluid under high pressure to adjust ride height, and seals deteriorate over time causing fluid loss. A complete system failure leaves the vehicle stuck at one height setting and triggers warning lights.
before.solution: Replace failed AHC components — actuators, accumulator, or hydraulic lines as needed. A complete AHC overhaul runs $3,000-$6,000 at the dealer. Alternatively, convert to a conventional spring suspension using aftermarket kits that eliminate all hydraulic components.
symptoms: Vehicle sits lower than normal on one or more corners
Height control switch no longer adjusts ride height
Hydraulic fluid leak visible under vehicle

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — LX570 AHC suspension failure patterns and conversion options

communityRecommendations.content: Budget for AHC maintenance on any LX570 over 80,000 miles. The system is shared with the Toyota Land Cruiser 200, so LC forums have extensive repair documentation that applies directly.

proposal.title: AHC (Active Height Control) Suspension Failure
proposal.description: Direct owner evidence confirms that an LX570 can lose AHC fluid and ride height, but the documented 2010 case was traced to a corroded, ruptured hydraulic line. Follow-up inspection showed that several initially suspected core hydraulic components did not need replacement. Other long-term LX owners describe AHC as robust or trouble-free. This evidence supports retaining the reported AHC failure identity, but not a claim that actuators, accumulators and lines generally fail across every 2008-2021 LX570.
proposal.solution: If an AHC warning, fluid leak or abnormal ride height appears, avoid repeatedly operating the height control and have a qualified technician locate the exact leak, read system faults and test hydraulic pressure and height-sensor operation. Repair only the verified line, sensor, pump, accumulator, actuator or related component under the model-year procedure. Do not authorize a complete overhaul or conventional-suspension conversion from this page alone. This is vehicle-specific hydraulic diagnosis; no universal retail part is asserted.

before.title: Brake Pedal Vibration / Front Brake Rotor Warping and Premature Brake Pulsation
before.description: A number of current-generation LX owners have complained of steering wheel shake or brake pedal pulsation during moderate-to-hard braking, often at relatively low mileage for a full-size luxury SUV. Reports point to front rotor thickness variation or heat-related rotor distortion, especially on heavy vehicles used in urban driving or towing. While not unique to Lexus, the issue is documented enough in owner discussions and complaints to be considered a known pattern on this generation.
before.solution: Road-test the vehicle to confirm pulsation, then measure rotor runout and thickness variation. Dealers or independent shops typically resurface or replace front rotors and pads; if the problem recurs, verify caliper slide operation, wheel torque uniformity, and bedding-in procedure. Upgraded pad compounds or higher-quality replacement rotors are often suggested by owners who experienced repeat issues.
symptoms: Vibration at highway speeds when slowing down

communityRecommendations.content: Owners often recommend checking wheel lug torque after tire service because uneven torque can worsen rotor runout.
If replacing parts out of pocket, many suggest premium coated rotors and ceramic pads rather than simply resurfacing factory rotors.

proposal.title: Brake Pedal Vibration / Front Brake Rotor Warping and Premature Brake Pulsation
proposal.description: The exact Lexus bulletin found for 2022-2025 LX600 vehicles, L-SB-0036-24 Rev1, addresses front-brake squeal while driving forward or in reverse. Its dealer procedure replaces specified front discs, pads, shims and related hardware for that squeal condition. It does not document brake-pedal vibration, rotor warping, thickness variation, towing or urban-use causation. Current exact evidence therefore does not substantiate the frozen pulsation identity as a generation-wide pattern.
proposal.solution: For a pulsation or steering-wheel shake, a qualified brake technician should reproduce the symptom, inspect wheel and hub mounting surfaces, verify wheel-fastener torque, measure disc runout and thickness variation, and check caliper operation before selecting parts. Use L-SB-0036-24 only when its front-squeal condition and applicability are met. Do not infer upgraded pads, higher-quality rotors or a bulletin repair for pulsation from this page. This is condition- and vehicle-specific brake diagnosis; no universal retail part is asserted.

before.title: Center Differential Lock Actuator Failure
before.description: The center differential lock actuator on the LX570 transfer case fails due to internal motor degradation and moisture intrusion. The actuator is responsible for engaging the center diff lock for off-road use, and when it fails, the lock cannot be engaged. This is the same basic design used on the Toyota Land Cruiser 200.
before.solution: Replace the center differential lock actuator motor assembly on the transfer case. The OEM Toyota part is recommended. After installation, perform a system initialization using a Toyota/Lexus diagnostic scanner. Test engagement on a loose surface in a straight line.
symptoms: Center diff lock will not engage when button is pressed
Center diff lock indicator light flashes and does not stay on
Clicking noise from transfer case area

citations.title: ClubLexus.com — LX570 center diff lock actuator replacement guide

communityRecommendations.content: Engage the center diff lock at least once a month to prevent the actuator from seizing due to inactivity. Even a 30-second engagement in a parking lot keeps the mechanism exercised.

proposal.title: Center Differential Lock Actuator Failure
proposal.description: A direct 2013 LX570 report documents an intermittently flashing center-differential-lock warning and a dealer diagnosis involving a sensor and wire harness. Other participants speculated that an actuator may eventually require replacement, but the thread does not establish one universal cause. No exact Lexus communication in the complete inventory documents internal motor degradation or moisture intrusion as a model-wide defect.
proposal.solution: Follow the owner-manual procedure for an incomplete lock or unlock operation, and if the indicator continues flashing have a Lexus-capable technician read four-wheel-drive faults and test the switch, wiring, sensor, actuator and control circuit before replacing anything. Perform any required calibration or initialization under the exact model-year repair procedure. Do not assume an actuator or attempt impact-based workarounds from forum advice. This is vehicle-specific four-wheel-drive diagnosis; no universal retail part is asserted.

before.title: Front Occupant Classification / Airbag Sensor Fault Triggering SRS Warning and Airbag Recall Repairs
before.description: Multiple 2022-2024 Lexus LX owners reported persistent SRS/airbag warning messages and dealer diagnoses related to the front passenger occupant classification system and related airbag components. This generation shares Toyota/Lexus safety-system campaigns affecting front seat occupant sensing and airbag readiness, and owners describe warning lights, repeated dealer visits, and concerns about whether the passenger airbag will deploy correctly. Because the issue directly affects restraint-system operation, it is considered high severity even when the repair itself is covered by recall or warranty.
before.solution: Scan the SRS system with a Toyota/Lexus-capable diagnostic tool and inspect the passenger seat weight/occupant classification components, seat harnesses, and any applicable recall campaign status by VIN. Dealers typically perform recall remedies, recalibration, or replacement of affected seat sensor/airbag-related parts, then clear codes and verify the occupant detection status with a seat calibration procedure. If the warning returns, wiring under the seat and connector tension should be checked carefully.
symptoms: Passenger airbag OFF/ON status behaving abnormally
Warning appears after moving front passenger seat
Repeated dealer visits for airbag-related faults

communityRecommendations.content: Before troubleshooting, check open recalls by VIN and avoid placing heavy items under the passenger seat that can stress connectors.
If the warning appears intermittently after seat movement, owners recommend documenting seat position changes and taking photos/video before dealer visits.

proposal.title: Front Occupant Classification / Airbag Sensor Fault Triggering SRS Warning and Airbag Recall Repairs
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 26V180 covers certain 2022-2024 Lexus LX vehicles whose front-passenger seat-frame assembly may have insufficient clearance between the seat frame and a stopper. Interference can cause the occupant-classification sensor to measure the passenger load incorrectly, which may result in an improper passenger-airbag deployment strategy. The recall report does not establish persistent warning messages or repeated dealer visits as the identifying symptom.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for recall 26V180. Lexus dealers will inspect the relevant seat parts and replace the front-passenger seat-frame assembly if necessary at no charge. Do not disturb under-seat restraint wiring or attempt sensor calibration from this page; unrelated SRS warnings still require code-based diagnosis under the exact service procedure. This is a VIN-specific safety-recall remedy; no retail part is asserted.

before.title: Power Tailgate / Rear Hatch Fails to Open or Close Properly Due to Latch or Strut/Module Faults
before.description: Owners have reported intermittent operation of the LX split rear hatch/power tailgate system, including failure to open, failure to cinch closed, or warning messages indicating the rear door is open when it appears latched. On a vehicle with a complex powered rear closure system, faults can stem from latch alignment, pinch sensors, control modules, or weak power strut behavior. The issue is inconvenient and can create security or battery-drain concerns if the vehicle thinks the hatch remains ajar.
before.solution: Inspect for stored body or back-door control codes, verify latch alignment, and test the power back-door motor/strut operation and anti-pinch sensors. Dealers may update control software, adjust the latch/striker, or replace the latch assembly or powered support components. If the hatch is intermittently reported open, check for water intrusion or connector issues in the rear door area.
symptoms: Tailgate starts to close then reverses
Rear door open warning stays on

communityRecommendations.content: Owners suggest cleaning and lightly lubricating the latch/striker area before assuming the power struts are bad.
If the hatch warning is intermittent, take photos of the cluster message and note whether it happens after rain or car washes.

proposal.title: Power Tailgate / Rear Hatch Fails to Open or Close Properly Due to Latch or Strut/Module Faults
proposal.description: Direct reports from 2023 and 2024 LX600 owners document an intermittent power tailgate that opens but will not close, gives two beeps and may work again at cooler times of day. In those reports, dealer diagnosis identified a sticking or failed pinch sensor and replacement restored operation. The evidence does not establish a model-wide latch, power-strut or control-module fault, nor the page's security, battery-drain or water-intrusion claims.
proposal.solution: Record the intermittent failure, check for an obstruction or damaged weatherstrip, and have a Lexus-capable technician read back-door faults and test both pinch sensors, alignment and the commanded close operation. Replace only the component confirmed by diagnosis under the exact model-year procedure. Do not assume the latch, struts or module from the symptom alone. This is vehicle-specific power-back-door diagnosis; no universal retail part is asserted.

before.title: V35A-FTS 3.4L Twin-Turbo V6 Main Bearing / Engine Failure Risk Covered by Toyota-Lexus Recall
before.description: The 2022+ Lexus LX uses the V35A-FTS twin-turbo V6 that is included in Toyota/Lexus campaigns for potential engine damage from machining debris and resulting main-bearing failure. Owners have reported knocking, reduced power, check-engine lights, and in some cases complete engine replacement. This is one of the most serious documented issues for the current LX because it can lead to sudden engine failure and very expensive repairs outside recall coverage.
before.solution: Check VIN for open engine recall/campaign status immediately. If symptoms such as knocking, low oil pressure warnings, or misfire/limp mode appear, the vehicle should not be driven until inspected; dealers may perform engine inspection and, where required by campaign procedure, short-block or complete engine replacement. Oil filter inspection for metallic debris and oil pressure verification are key diagnostic steps.
symptoms: Engine failure or no-start after internal damage

citations.title: NHTSA recall query - Toyota/Lexus V35A-FTS engine failure / debris-related campaign affecting Lexus LX

communityRecommendations.content: Owners recommend checking recall status by VIN regularly and requesting documentation of any engine inspection or replacement performed.
If buying used, ask for oil analysis or service records showing recall completion and use of correct oil spec.

proposal.title: V35A-FTS 3.4L Twin-Turbo V6 Main Bearing / Engine Failure Risk Covered by Toyota-Lexus Recall
proposal.description: NHTSA recall 25V767 expands the earlier 24V381 population and covers certain 2022-2024 Lexus LX vehicles with a specific V35A engine configuration. Manufacturing debris may contaminate the engine and cause the number-one main bearing to wear or fail, which can lead to engine stall and loss of drive power. The recall population is VIN- and production-specific; the report does not make every V35A engine defective or identify knocking, low-oil-pressure warnings and misfires as the required screening method.
proposal.solution: Check the VIN for recall 25V767 and arrange the free Lexus dealer remedy. Dealers use inspection software and collected vehicle data to evaluate the number-one main bearing; if the software cannot confirm that the bearing is free from abnormal wear, the dealer replaces the engine at no charge. Do not prescribe oil-filter inspection, a short block or automatic engine replacement outside that campaign procedure. This is a VIN-specific safety-recall remedy; no retail part is asserted.
